outputs.prompt: Create a whiskey bottle lying horizontally on its side on the floor of the cabin in the 1899 adventure game. First reference is the original bottle: preserve its low elongated silhouette, orientation, perspective, proportions and dominant colors. Broad dark olive-green glass body at the left, shoulders tapering to a narrow neck pointing right, small brown cork/cap at the far right; muted pale olive-cream rectangular label on the body. Preserve this simple readable design; refine the glass with restrained highlights and purposeful finer clusters, and make the label legible as a small plain label without invented branding or lettering. The subject should occupy seven eighths of the square composition's width and three eighths of its height, lying level with a consistent lower floor contact. Second reference, Churchill, is ONLY a reference for finer detail, restrained shading and dark outline treatment, never for anatomy, clothing, pose or colors. Third reference, approved quill and inkwell, guides the outline and small-object detail only; do not add a feather or inkwell. Fourth reference contains the common 128-color palette swatches: use these only as a flexible base for harmonious colors, allowing additional shades where useful; do not draw swatches. Give the bottle a continuous very dark outline exactly one final-image pixel thick, uniform around its silhouette, with stepped diagonals, no doubled border, halo, blur or antialiasing. Keep internal lines subtle and subordinate. Preserve source transparency with binary alpha. Bottle alone, no floor plane, no cast shadow extending the silhouette, no other props. Preserve the original floor contact and recognizable broad body and short narrow right-facing neck.
